title: F60 reduction changes the represented value for partial base factors
evidence: reduce divides num by gcd(num,60^scale), but decrements scale only for whole factors of 60 (lines 43–51).
trigger: BA.EXACT dividing numerator 2 by 60 produces F60::new(2,1); gcd=2 divides numerator to 1 without changing scale.
impact: The result becomes 1/60 instead of 1/30; ordinary exact arithmetic is silently corrupted.

title: Division ignores the denominator scale
evidence: BA.EXACT reads numerator register scale but only val2.num; val2.scale is never applied (326–337).
trigger: Divide integer 1 by register containing 1/60 (obtainable by dividing 1 by 60).
impact: Returns 1 rather than 60, corrupting any subsequent arithmetic on fractional operands.

title: Replay digest authenticates only elapsed ticks
evidence: initial hash is constant BABYLON-60-INIT and replay_hash is SHA256(self.c.to_be_bytes()); trace/state bytes never enter either hash (184–192).
trigger: Run different programs or change a traced opcode while preserving final tick count.
impact: Exported proof artifacts have identical replay hashes despite different programs/states; the hash cannot establish replay integrity.

title: Unsupported instructions are silently accepted
evidence: Opcode match fallback is _ => {}; execution then records opcode and advances PC (416–430). Assigned tools/examples/navier_stokes_hunter.b60 uses DAH, LAL, NU at lines 34,43,46, none implemented in this match.
trigger: Run the supplied Navier–Stokes script or mistype an opcode.
impact: Program silently skips arithmetic and branch operations; the supplied example cannot detect its advertised threshold.

title: Script operands can panic the interpreter outside its halt path
evidence: ALLOC unconditionally indexes tokens[1], tokens[2] and coro.r[idx]; similar unchecked reads appear in other opcodes. Register file length is 64 (455).
trigger: Script contains ALLOC alone or ALLOC F60 R64.
impact: Out-of-bounds panic terminates the process without critical_halt/export_artifact diagnostics.

title: TLOAD is decoded as 0x5e instead of 0x5c
evidence: OPCODE_TLOAD = 0x5C + 2 is counted at lines 223-224; EIP-1153 specifies TLOAD=0x5c and TSTORE=0x5d (https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-1153). bounty_pipeline_orchestrator.py:117,130-145 consumes these results for risk-based receipts.
trigger: Analyze bytecode containing 5c or 5e.
impact: Actual transient reads are missed and unrelated 0x5e instructions are labeled transient reads; balance heuristics and risk receipts become incorrect.

title: Hook permissions use the most significant address bits
evidence: bits = (addr_int >> (160 - 14)) & 0x3FFF; official Hooks.sol uses the least significant bits (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Uniswap/v4-core/main/src/libraries/Hooks.sol). analyze_bytecode consumes before_swap and delta flags at lines 287-299.
trigger: A hook address ends with 0080 while its high bits are zero, or high bits are set with low hook bits absent.
impact: Misses active BEFORE_SWAP and misattributes unrelated address bits as permissions, changing downstream risk decisions.

title: Require digest coverage for every required evidence file
evidence: signed_file_digests defaults to {}; only supplied entries are hashed at lines 904–924. required_rel_files is checked for existence only. CLI consumes valid as PASS and exit 0 (verifier/cli.py:89–95).
trigger: A pack has a signed envelope omitting claims.json, scope.json, regulatory matrix or other required files from file_digests.
impact: Omitted files can be changed without invalidating signature/checksums; checksums_valid can still be true and mutable claims affect final verdict.

title: Reject an empty execution trace for a nonempty ledger
evidence: All count/hash comparisons are nested under if trace_lines; an empty trace skips the promised cross-check.
trigger: Pack contains a nonempty valid ledger and an empty execution-trace.jsonl with matching updated signed file digest.
impact: Verifier reports evidence verifiable despite no execution trace corresponding to the ledger.

title: Failed commit is retried with hooks disabled
evidence: run_git_sentinel retries every nonzero git commit using --no-verify. add-objective/add-milestone/update-status/iter call it at lines 159,196,225,270.
trigger: A pre-commit or commit-msg policy hook rejects an objective change.
impact: The automatic retry can commit the rejected tree without its validation hooks.

title: Objective commands stage unrelated work
evidence: run_git_sentinel runs git add . from WORKSPACE_DIR before committing; callers mutate the objectives YAML and optionally PROJECT.md.
trigger: Run an objective mutation while unrelated tracked edits or nonignored untracked files exist.
impact: Unrelated work is staged and committed under the objective message, potentially capturing private or unfinished files.

title: Sexagesimal conversion silently truncates the high limb
evidence: from_decimal casts value / 3600 to u32; saturating_add delegates to this conversion.
trigger: from_decimal(3600 * 2**32), or adding one to the maximum canonical three-limb value.
impact: The value wraps to zero instead of rejecting or saturating; ordering and computed bounds become incorrect.

title: Saturating radius loses the claimed interval enclosure
evidence: add_ball and sub_ball use u32::saturating_add for uncertainty radii.
trigger: Add two F60Ball values centered at zero with radius u32::MAX each.
impact: The mathematical sum can reach 2*u32::MAX but returned upper_bound is only u32::MAX; contains falsely excludes valid results.

title: Timeout is reported as a successful zero-copy falsification
evidence: Timeout at lines 52-54 breaks the loop, then lines 56-60 unconditionally print FALSACIÓN PYTHON ZERO-COPY SUPERADA; main returns normally.
trigger: No orchestrator tasks arrive within 60 seconds, or fewer than ten arrive.
impact: The PoC exits successfully and prints a passing result without reaching its own ten-task completion condition.

title: Shutdown stops before draining accepted transactions
evidence: shutdown sets _stop_event before awaiting writer; loop condition at line 54 exits when set. Sentinel does not override that condition.
trigger: Submit transactions then immediately await shutdown, before writer drains queue.
impact: Accepted auxiliary database writes can be lost while shutdown logs clean completion; queued task counts remain unfinished.

title: TCW classifier omits required flanking nucleotide
evidence: Forward branch checks middle C and final A/T but never motif[0] == T; reverse branch checks middle G and first A/T but never final A. Docstring at 88 specifies TCW.
trigger: Pass C>T with context ACA or CCA, or G>A with TGC.
impact: Non-TCW variants are counted as TCW and can change reported enrichment and is_apobec_driven. This finding concerns implemented string predicate, without clinical efficacy claims.

title: Failed email handlers are acknowledged and permanently deduplicated
evidence: is_duplicate inserts the message ID before handlers execute (lines 191-204); lines 255-259 swallow handler exceptions and return status processed; router returns this result at lines 309-310.
trigger: A registered synchronous handler raises while processing a webhook with message_id.
impact: HTTP success suppresses provider retries; an explicit retry is duplicate_skipped for the TTL although the handler never completed. Track completion and report failure before acknowledging.

title: Blackboard resolution is not an atomic OPEN transition
evidence: resolve reads and checks OPEN at 288-292, then UPDATE uses only WHERE tuple_id = ? and commits. Independent CortexWalStore connections use the same SQLite database.
trigger: Two processes read the same OPEN tuple before either resolution commits.
impact: Both can succeed and the later resolution overwrites the first status, verifier and evidence, violating the documented OPEN-only state transition.

title: Guide directs broad automatic commits and contradicts current commit contract
evidence: Step 3 says execute immediate atomic commits and shows git add . && git commit -m "feat(module): description [Causal-Determinist]"; AGENTS.md requires preserving others work and authorized commits with [AX-<Num>] format.
trigger: An agent/operator follows this workflow guide for an ordinary edit on a dirty checkout.
impact: Unrelated changes can be staged and committed; the guide also encourages publication-adjacent Git mutation without establishing authorization. This is conflicting documentation, not evidence it was executed.

title: Attestation summary counts disagree with taxonomy
evidence: UNTESTED array has seven entries (23–29), while matrix_counts.untested=5 and total_claims=21 (37–41). Arrays contain 12 supported + 2 falsified + 7 untested + 2 unfalsifiable = 23.
trigger: Consume matrix_counts as the bundle coverage summary.
impact: Consumers undercount untested claims and total scope. This finding concerns internal consistency only; stored test claims were not independently reproduced.

title: I/O demo deletes a preexisting database in the working directory
evidence: db_path is the fixed relative name falsacion_agentes.db; existing file is removed before opening, and removed again at line 29.
trigger: Run the demo in a directory containing a database with that name.
impact: Existing user data is irreversibly removed; use an owned temporary file.

title: Code generation records uncompiled rules as compiled and active
evidence: After writing Rust, lines 191–205 insert execution_time_ns=180000 and update status=COMPILED without invoking a compiler or timing execution. destiladora_schema.sql lines 55–60 describe measured latency and default active_in_ring0=1; test_destiladora_e2e.py only invokes cargo later at line 133.
trigger: Run generate_rust_fastpath with a proved cluster, including one whose generated Rust fails compilation.
impact: Persistent rule metadata advertises compilation, activation and measured execution time before those facts are established, and remains so if the later compilation fails.

title: Non-JSON quality gate returns success when leaked artifacts are its only failure
evidence: success is false at line 131 for leaked_artifacts; JSON mode returns it at 150, but text mode checks only violations at 163-169 and unconditionally returns True at 173.
trigger: Run audit_scripts_quality.py without --json with valid Python scripts and a disallowed non-hidden artifact in scripts/.
impact: CLI exits zero and prints ALL SCRIPTS PASSED despite reporting an artifact leak; pre-commit/CI callers can accept a failed gate.

title: Forensic report certifies controls without checking them
evidence: Cohort 5 agent 99 unconditionally assigns PASS and ATTESTED_C5_REAL. Agents 64-70 and 83-86 similarly return static security/integrity claims. compile_swarm_sitrep derives an exergy score from PASS count at line 380. Auditor.py:757-779 schedules these functions and persists their results.
trigger: Any invocation of the conversation auditor, including a corpus containing leaks, broken links or divergent files.
impact: Persisted reports falsely attest unchecked controls; the final certification remains PASS regardless of the failed findings in other agents.

title: Entropy gate labels agreement as safe without checking correctness
evidence: cluster_samples groups identical nonempty texts together; H is then zero. Lines 80-94 label that result safe and return True; no correctness or evidence predicate exists. Line 152 additionally claims isolated memory and guaranteed fail-stop from repeated string fixtures.
trigger: Supply two or more identical false or unsafe answers.
impact: The PoC accepts the samples and prints a safe-transition verdict even though it has only measured lexical agreement. These verdicts cannot establish hallucination blocking or isolation.

title: Correct the attojoule scaling of the Landauer constants
evidence: The file states 2.87e-21 J/bit at lines 10-14 and names the unit aJ*1000, but assigns 2870 and total 1102080 at 36/44. Since 1 aJ=1e-18 J, 2.87e-21 J is 0.00287 aJ, or 2.87 aJ*1000, not 2870. aphairesis_entropy_loss_aj_x1000 multiplies this constant at 121.
trigger: A caller uses the exported aJ*1000 constants or aphairesis_entropy_loss_aj_x1000 according to their documented units.
impact: Computed energy floors are overstated by approximately 1000x; compile-time assertions merely enforce the same erroneous scale. This is a numerical/unit finding, not an empirical energy measurement.

title: Preaggregation example loses almost all events
evidence: buffer is initialized to zero in the snippet, then written only if Date.now() % 1000 === 0; there is no timer, retained batch, or unconditional flush.
trigger: Use the shown solution during requests that do not land on the exact millisecond divisible by 1000.
impact: Most requests emit no data point; the example does not implement its claimed once-per-second aggregation.

title: Make Channel Rack CC ranges disjoint
evidence: Selection checks cc_num < chan_count before mute range 16 <= cc_num <16+chan_count and solo range 32 <= cc_num <32+chan_count.
trigger: A project has 17 or more channels and receives channel-7 CC16 to mute channel0; with 33 channels CC32 is likewise consumed by selection.
impact: Mute/solo commands select a different channel or mute an unintended channel instead of performing the requested operation.

title: Generated Python CI masks every pytest failure
evidence: generate_ci_scaffold("python") emits python -m pytest || true. CLI --scaffold-ci prints that template at 313-315.
trigger: A user adopts the generated Python workflow and pytest fails or cannot import.
impact: The test step succeeds despite failing tests, making the scaffold unsuitable as a failing quality gate.

title: Monitor presents constants as live security and treasury telemetry
evidence: load_telemetry_data hardcodes allocation=46.66, gate LOCKED, ring0 NOMINAL, oracle ARMED (51–54); only DB/manifests/calendar are read (57–87). UI adds biometric status, <15ns latency and total legal compliance (126–129).
trigger: Run --once with missing inputs or a failed/unavailable gate.
impact: Operator receives successful-looking hardware/security/compliance status and treasury allocation without observations from those systems; failures cannot change these indicators.
